extracted.intended_audience: new mathematics instructors and graduate teaching assistants (TAs)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and checklists for running pre-semester training and in-class cooperative learning activities for introductory college mathematics instructors and TAs. Covers homework team roles, selecting and managing cooperative in-class activities, meeting preparation, and evaluation items for orientation sessions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scribe (homework team role)
rubrics_metrics.description: The scribe is responsible for writing up the single final version of the homework to be handed in. This is the set of solutions that will be graded. Each member of the team will receive the same grade.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Whenever possible solutions should include symbolic, graphical, and verbal explanations or interpretations. Diagrams and pictures should also be provided whenever possible. The homework should be neatly written or typed, and stapled or paper-clipped.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarifier (homework team role)
rubrics_metrics.description: The clarifier is responsible for assisting the team by paraphrasing the ideas presented by the other team members and making sure everyone in the team understands the solutions before the team moves on.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The role is emphasized as the most important for ensuring group understanding, though often neglected; focus on shared understanding rather than individual answers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporter (homework team role)
rubrics_metrics.description: The reporter writes a record of how the homework sessions went: where, when, and how long the team met; what difficulties or successes the team had; and lists members who attended and their roles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The report should note absences, be on a separate sheet of paper, and be the first page of the homework.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manager (homework team role)
rubrics_metrics.description: The manager arranges and runs the meetings, ensures all members know where and when the meeting will take place, and manages distribution of materials when homework is returned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If only three members attend, the manager should take the role of the missing person. If willing, the manager should arrange refreshments. When homework is returned the manager should see that it is photocopied and distributed to each member.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forming initial homework teams (procedure)
rubrics_metrics.description: A method for creating initial homework teams at the start of the semester.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Steps: gather completed student data forms; collate forms into piles by first-preference meeting time; put students into groups of four by campus proximity; try to make groups heterogeneous by gender, year, major, mathematical experiences, ability, and attitudes; move some students to second-preference piles if necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instructor states the topic clearly
rubrics_metrics.description: Instructor states the topic clearly at the beginning of an explanation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of 'Material and content' analysis for explanations; signaling the topic primes student attention and frames the lesson.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explanation is organized
rubrics_metrics.description: The explanation is organized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organization helps students follow argument and see logical progression; evaluate structure and transitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasize the main idea
rubrics_metrics.description: Instructor emphasizes the main idea of the explanation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlight central points explicitly so students recognize key takeaways rather than getting lost in details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relate material to prior knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: Instructor relates material to something students already know.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use connections to prior knowledge to scaffold understanding and make new concepts more accessible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Give suitable examples
rubrics_metrics.description: Instructor gives suitable examples.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples should concretize abstract points and span typical and edge cases where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate level of material
rubrics_metrics.description: The material is appropriate to the level of beginning undergraduates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Match depth and pace to audience; avoid assuming too much or too little background.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide a clear conclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Instructor has a clear conclusion to the explanation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Summarize essential points and connections to larger goals or upcoming material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Involve students
rubrics_metrics.description: Instructor involves students in the explanation (Technique and delivery).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Active involvement promotes engagement and peer explanation; use questions, small tasks, or group prompts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Show enthusiasm
rubrics_metrics.description: The instructor shows enthusiasm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enthusiasm can motivate student interest and signal importance of material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board work clarity and readability
rubrics_metrics.description: Board work is clearly organized and readable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Neat, structured board work supports student note-taking and following logical steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate pace
rubrics_metrics.description: The pace of presentation is appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjust speed to student comprehension; allow time for processing and questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Orientation session evaluation checklist (Blocks A–C)
rubrics_metrics.description: A collection of evaluation items used to assess orientation sessions, including clarity of goals, distinction between student-centered vs presentation approaches, usefulness of lesson-planning guidance, competence with tools, and session management.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific items include: goals clearly described; differences between student-centered and lecture explained; lesson-planning contributions to course goals; competence with graphing calculator; ability to design grading system; knowledge of documents for first day; session stayed on topic/schedule; procedures for grouping students and homework teams; awareness of cooperative learning management and difficulties; recognition of quizzes' roles and typical length/difficulty; practice teaching opportunities and feedback usefulness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose activities that require group work
rubrics_metrics.description: Select problems that truly require and encourage students to work in groups — i.e., problems where there is a discernible difference between tasks for individuals and tasks for groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether the problem is too easily partitioned, whether it naturally benefits from multiple viewpoints, and whether group interaction is necessary for success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose activities aligned with learning goals
rubrics_metrics.description: Choose problems that facilitate the particular learning goals the instructor has for that portion of the lesson.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When planning, explicitly identify what you want students to learn from each problem and design or select tasks to achieve those goals; connect tasks to lesson and course objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Good features of cooperative activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Features that make a problem conducive to extended cooperative learning activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes: too hard to do alone; ill-structured; more than one answer; useful to have multiple ideas or viewpoints; requiring interpretation or synthesis of concepts; requiring multiple ideas or viewpoints; requires symbolic/graphical/verbal synthesis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bad features of cooperative activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Features that make a problem not conducive to extended cooperative learning activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes: too easy; mostly computational; calculator too much of a focus (becomes a barrier); easy to split into parts or 'divvy up' so individuals can work separately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instructor behaviors for successful in-class cooperative activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Behaviors the instructor should exhibit to contribute significantly to the success of cooperative learning activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key behaviors: give clear directions on the activity; give clear instructions on how/where groups should form and what to work on; set a definite pace and time frame; visit groups and give suggestions as they work; require students to explain answers when wrapping up; briefly list vital points touched on when concluding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mechanics for starting group activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Practical steps to initiate a group activity effectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give very clear instructions and expected product (write on board/overhead); ask one person per group to read the problem aloud; occasionally ask groups to present at the blackboard; do a quick initial tour to identify off-task groups and reiterate tasks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dealing with off-task behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: Strategies for identifying and correcting groups that are off-task during activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If persistent off-task behavior occurs, reassign groups (count off, alphabetically, birth date). Encourage groups by asking them which parts they've done, warning they'll be called on, or having them move to the board. Plan additional tasks for groups that finish early.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time management for group activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Strategies for managing time during group work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Communicate allotted time in advance; break long multi-part activities into sections and discuss intermediate parts to keep pace; appoint a facilitator in each group to help keep schedule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facilitating the group process (ground rules and logistics)
rubrics_metrics.description: Instructor practices that facilitate productive group interactions and process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be proactive: establish and communicate ground rules; arrange seating to encourage face-to-face interaction; do not tolerate off-task behavior; defer grading/administrative questions to other forums; avoid monopolizing time with one group; acknowledge stuck groups and return promptly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meeting preparation checklist
rubrics_metrics.description: Preparation steps for a training meeting on in-class group work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose five or six representative textbook problems (including at least one poor example), consult experienced cooperative-learning instructors, gather a panel of experienced instructors if possible, circulate agenda in advance, make copies of materials and questionnaires, and confirm attendance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uses for short and long in-class cooperative activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Suggested pedagogical uses for short versus longer cooperative activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Short activities: check work on a routine problem, clarify a concept through peer explanation, generate ideas when class is stuck. Longer activities: introduce concepts or skills, clarify concepts or skills, practice and review concepts or skills. Plan to intersperse short activities with brief lectures (<=10 minutes).
